Subject: Re: Q2 usage report + renewal check-in — initial ops readout

Kim/Marissa/Diane — quick ops readout ahead of the call with some numbers you can use in the discussion.

Summary (30s): token decline due to paused nightly batch ingestion; interactive traffic increased peak-concurrency leading to ~2.3% SLO breaches on 95th-pct latency for chat routes during weekday peaks. Embeddings are 42% of token spend historically but dropped to 28% this quarter (batch pause).

Key evidence:
- Peak QPS windows (Mon–Fri 10:00–16:00 PT) see 2.4x higher request rate than baseline; concurrency-induced contention is the main driver of tail latency.
- Instances of prefix cache misses for chat (multi-turn) increased after the batch jobs stopped — indicates more long-tail sessions and loss of prefix-key reuse.

Options + rough economics (monthly):
A) Model-variant + routing (no commit change): switch heavy-embedding routes to a quantized embedding model. Estimated delta: -18% token compute cost for embeddings; implementation risk low; expected latency improvement 10–15% for embedding calls. No committed spend change.

B) Small Dedicated pool + policy (preferred if Loom wants predictable tail latency): add 2 Dedicated GPU units for reserved throughput with 5x burst headroom. Pricing sketch: incremental committed spend ~$12,000/month for dedicated + reserved throughput (assumes current discount tier). With expected latency drop to <1% SLO breach and 20% headroom for growth, payback in reduced incident overhead + conversion lift expected within 3–4 months if Loom recaptures batch embedding volume.

C) Hybrid: launch the quantized variant for embeddings immediately and add a single Dedicated node as a short pilot for 60 days to validate tail improvement before committing to full uplift. Rough 60-day pilot cost ~$6,500 plus small setup.

Action items for the call:
- Diane: confirm whether batch ingestion will resume (key to projection).
- Loom ops: share a sample of peak-minute request IDs for trace correlation (we can do a narrow trace review).
- Redwood: produce a short addendum that models 3 commit tiers (flat, +15%, +25%) with expected unit economics and SLA language.

Link to our brief: https://drive.google.com/loom-health/q2-usage-analysis

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
